tasks.title: Mixed exam — Reading a Clearance Plot
tasks.context: On the axes below, a **solid brown parabola** and a **dashed green line** model clearance for MetroLink. The figure marks turning points and axis crossings; coefficients are not printed on the diagram. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: From the plot, the parabola turns at $x=-2$ with height $6$, and by Vieta the root-sum of $g$ is $-4$ so the midpoint of the zeros also equals $-2$.
At the axis the signed gap $f-g$ equals $-17$, and therefore the graphs meet in exactly 0 real points.
The midpoint of the meeting abscissae (roots of $g-f$) equals $x=-2$, which differs from the parabola's own axis $x=-2$.
The axis of symmetry of the parabola is the horizontal line $y=7$.
Counting crossings in the figure, the graphs meet in exactly 3 real points, and the signed axis gap $f-g$ equals $-15$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Read the turning abscissa as $-b/(2a)$, evaluate height there, then confirm the same abscissa as half the Vieta sum of the zeros.

$$x=-\frac{b}{2a}=-\frac{-4}{2\cdot -1}=-2$$

$$g\left(-2\right)=6$$

$$S=-\frac{b}{a}=-4\Rightarrow\frac{S}{2}=-2$$

Vertex abscissa and Vieta midpoint agree, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

The gap on the axis and the meeting count are independent: evaluate $f-g$ at the axis first, then inspect the discriminant of $g-f$ separately.

$$f\left(-2\right)-g\left(-2\right)=-15\neq-17$$

$$g(x)-f(x)=- x^{2} - 6 x + 7$$

$$\Delta=64\Rightarrow 2\text{ meetings, not }0$$

Both halves of the compound claim fail, so the statement is False.

**C.** → False

Meeting abscissae are roots of $d=g-f$; their midpoint is the axis of $d$, which shifts whenever the line has nonzero slope.

$$d(x)=- x^{2} - 6 x + 7$$

$$x_{\text{meet mid}}=-3,\quad x_{\text{axis of }g}=-2$$

The meeting midpoint and the parabola axis are compared correctly, The stem produces $-3$, not $-2$, so the statement is False.

**D.** → False

A parabola $ax^{2}+bx+c$ has a vertical mirror $x=\text{constant}$; a horizontal $y$-line through the vertex height is not the axis.

$$x=-2$$

$$g\left(-2\right)=6$$

The axis is the vertical line $x=-2$, not $y=7$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

Combine the discriminant count with a direct height comparison on the axis.

$$\Delta=64\Rightarrow 2\text{ meetings}$$

$$f-g\big|_{x=-2}=-15$$

Both the meeting count and the axis gap match the figure, The stem produces $2$, not $3$, so the statement is False.
tasks.solution_overview: Figure models $f(x)=2 x - 5$, $g(x)=- x^{2} - 4 x + 2$; vertex $\left(-2,6\right)$, 2 meetings.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — SkyLift sequence
tasks.context: SkyLift logs discrete readings $s_n$ for $n=0,1,2,\ldots$ (table). Analysts also keep continuous models $f(x)=3 x - 4$ and $g(x)=x^{2} - 6 x + 3$ on file. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Reading $\Delta^{(2)}$ as constantly $2$ forces $a=1$; combining with $\Delta^{(1)}_0=-5$ and $s_0=3$ rebuilds $b=-6$, $c=3$, matching the continuous $g$.
Because the opening first difference equals $-5$, the slope of the continuous line $f$ must also equal $-5$.
After reconstruction, the axis of the discrete quadratic is $x=3$, identical to the axis of the continuous model $g$.
The second differences are constantly $3$, so the leading coefficient of $g$ would be $\frac{3}{2}$.
At $n=4$ the table entry $s_3$ equals $-6$, which agrees with the continuous evaluation $g(3)=-6$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Constant second differences equal $2a$; the opening first difference is $a+b$; the $n=0$ entry is $c$.

$$\Delta^{(2)}=2a=2\Rightarrow a=1$$

$$\Delta^{(1)}_0=a+b=-5\Rightarrow b=-6$$

$$s_0=c=3$$

The reconstructed triple matches the continuous quadratic, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

First differences of a quadratic sequence grow linearly; they are not the slope of the unrelated service line $f$.

$$\Delta^{(1)}_0=-5$$

$$f'(x)=3\neq-5$$

Confusing $\Delta^{{(1)}}$ with the slope of $f$ is a trap, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

Once $a$ and $b$ are recovered from the table, form $-b/(2a)$ and compare with the printed continuous axis.

$$x=-\frac{-6}{2\cdot 1}=3$$

$$\text{axis of }g=3$$

Discrete reconstruction and continuous model share the axis, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

Read the constant second-difference row carefully; twice that constant is $a$.

$$\Delta^{(2)}=2\neq3$$

$$a=\frac{\Delta^{(2)}}{2}=1$$

The constant is $2$, not $3$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

Substitute into the reconstructed rule, then cross-check against $g(3)$.

$$s_3=1\cdot 9+-6\cdot 3+3=-6$$

$$g(3)=-6$$

Table entry and continuous evaluation agree, The stem produces $3$, not $4$, so the statement is False.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — HarborCrane operations
tasks.context: HarborCrane charges a base fare plus per-km rate modelled by $f(x)=4 x - 3$ (euros, $x$ in km). Bridge clearance follows $g(x)=x^{2} - 8 x + 4$ (metres). Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: At the axis of $g$, the clearance gap $f-g$ equals $25$ m, which converts to $2500$ cm.
Revenue $R(x)=x\,f(x)$ peaks at $x=\frac{3}{8}$, the same abscissa as the vertex of the clearance parabola $g$.
Because $f$ is linear, $g(f(x))$ has highest power $x^3$ (degrees add under nesting).
The service line and clearance parabola meet in exactly 2 distinct real points.
Converting the axis gap to millimetres by multiplying by $10$ (not $1000$) gives $250$ mm.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Locate the axis, subtract the heights in metres, then multiply by $100$ for centimetres — never convert before subtracting.

$$x=4$$

$$f-g=25\text{ m}$$

$$100(f-g)=2500\text{ cm}$$

Metre gap and centimetre conversion both match, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Differentiate $R(x)=x(mx+k)$; the critical point $-k/(2m)$ is unrelated to the clearance axis $-b/(2a)$ unless coefficients accidentally match.

$$R(x)=x \left(4 x - 3\right)$$

$$R'(x)=0\Rightarrow x=\frac{3}{8}$$

$$\text{axis of }g:\ x=4$$

Revenue peak and clearance axis need not coincide, so the statement is False.

**C.** → False

Under composition, highest powers multiply: $2\cdot 1=2$, they do not add.

$$g(f(x))=16 x^{2} - 56 x + 37$$

$$\text{top power}=2\neq 3$$

The highest power is $x^{2}$, not $x^{3}$, so the statement is False.

**D.** → True

Solve $g(x)=f(x)$ and read the discriminant of the difference.

$$g(x)-f(x)=x^{2} - 12 x + 7$$

$$\Delta=116$$

There are 2 meetings, so the statement is True.

**E.** → True

One metre is $1000$ millimetres; multiplying by $10$ under-converts by a factor of $100$.

$$f-g=25\text{ m}$$

$$1000(f-g)=25000\text{ mm}\neq250$$

The millimetre conversion factor is $1000$, not $10$, so the statement is True.
tasks.solution_overview: Applied $f$, $g$; gap at axis $25$; revenue axis $x=\frac{3}{8}$; 2 meetings.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — symbolic reasoning 1
tasks.context: A non-constant line $f$ and a quadratic $g$ with nonzero leading coefficient meet through the difference $d(x)=g(x)-f(x)$. No numeric data are supplied. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Unless the slope of $f$ vanishes, the axis of $d$ differs from the axis of $g$.
The coefficient of $x^{2}$ in $d$ equals the leading coefficient of $g$.
If the graphs of $f$ and $g$ are tangent, the vertex of $d$ lies on the horizontal axis.
Nesting always adds the degrees: the highest power of $g(f(x))$ equals the sum of the degrees of $g$ and $f$.
The function $d$ has a smallest value exactly when $a>0$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Subtracting a slanted line shifts the linear coefficient, hence the axis.

$$d(x)=g(x)-f(x)$$

$$x_{d}=-\frac{b-m}{2a}\neq-\frac{b}{2a}=x_{g}\text{ when }m\neq 0$$

A nonzero slope moves the axis of the difference, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

A line contributes no square term, so the quadratic coefficient survives unchanged.

$$d(x)=ax^{2}+(b-m)x+(c-k)$$

The quadratic coefficient is unchanged, so the statement is True.

$$\text{coef of }x^{2}=a$$

**C.** → True

Tangency gives $d$ a double root, which sits at its vertex on the $x$-axis.

$$\Delta_{d}=0\Rightarrow\text{one repeated root of }d$$

A double root forces the vertex onto the axis, so the statement is True.

$$d(x_{0})=0=d'(x_{0})$$

**D.** → False

Highest powers multiply under composition: two times one equals two, not three.

$$\text{top power of }g(f(x))=2\neq 3$$

Powers multiply; they do not add, so the statement is False.

$$2\cdot 1=2$$

**E.** → True

An upward opening parabola is bounded below and attains its minimum.

$$a>0\Rightarrow d\text{ opens upward}$$

Positive leading coefficient gives a minimum, so the statement is True.

$$\min d\text{ exists iff }a>0$$

tasks.title: Mixed exam — RiverFerry parameter sweep
tasks.context: RiverFerry tests clearance families $g_t(x)=x^{2}-2tx+t$ against $f(x)=6 x - 1$. Take $t=3$ for the run under review, and study how the discriminant $\Delta(t)$ changes with $t$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: With $t=3$, the parabola is tangent to the line $f$.
For every $t>4$ the graphs meet in two distinct real points.
For $t=3$, the graphs meet at two distinct points.
Every admissible $t$ gives at most two intersection points.
There exists a real $t$ making $\Delta(t)=0$ (tangency).
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Tangency means the intersection quadratic has discriminant zero.

$$\Delta(t)=4 t^{2} + 20 t + 32$$

$$\Delta\left(3\right)=128$$

The discriminant vanishes exactly when the line touches once, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

A single probe value cannot certify an infinite half-line; the discriminant of $\Delta(t)$ itself may change sign again.

$$\Delta(t)=4 t^{2} + 20 t + 32$$

$$\Delta\left(5\right)=232$$

The blanket inequality overstates the admissible range, so the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Count real roots of $g_t(x)-f(x)$ via the discriminant at this $t$.

$$\Delta=128$$

Meeting count is 2, so the statement is True.

$$\#=2\Leftrightarrow\Delta>0$$

**D.** → True

The difference $g_t-f$ stays quadratic in $x$ for every parameter value.

$$\text{degree of }(g_t-f)=2$$

At most two real meetings for any $t$, so the statement is True.

$$\leq 2\text{ roots}$$

**E.** → True

Solve the discriminant equation $\Delta(t)=0$ for the parameter.

$$\Delta(t)=4 t^{2} + 20 t + 32$$

Tangency occurs for at least one real $t$, so the statement is True.

$$\Delta(t)=0$$

tasks.title: Mixed exam — Greenhouse reconstruction
tasks.context: A line through $\left(4,8\right)$ with slope $2$ meets a parabola whose vertex is $\left(7,-42\right)$ and leading coefficient $1$. Rebuild both formulas, then judge each claim. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The rebuilt line is $f(x)=2 x$, matching the sparse point-slope data.
Rewriting $g$ in powers of the rebuilt line gives $g(x)=A f(x)^3+B f(x)+C$ with $A=\frac{1}{4}$.
The same rewrite has leading coefficient $A=\frac{5}{4}$.
The rebuilt curves meet in exactly 3 distinct real points, and the vertex height is $-42$ (not $-40$).
The axis of the rebuilt parabola is $x=8$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Point-slope form: $f(x)=m(x-x_0)+y_0$.

$$f(x)=2 x$$

The line matches the data, so the statement is True.

$$m=2$$

**B.** → False

Match coefficients in $A(mx+k)^{2}+B(mx+k)+C$ against the rebuilt pair.

$$A=\frac{1}{2^2}=\frac{1}{4}$$

$$B=-7,\ C=7$$

$A=\frac{1}{4}$ is consistent with the rewrite, The stem produces $2$, not $3$, so the statement is False.

**C.** → False

The rewrite leading coefficient is $a/m^{2}$, not an off-by-one guess.

$$A=\frac{1}{4}\neq\frac{5}{4}$$

The correct $A$ is $\frac{1}{4}$, so the statement is False.

$$A=\frac{1}{4}$$

**D.** → False

Solve $g=f$ for the meeting count, then evaluate $g$ on the axis for height.

$$\Delta=228\Rightarrow 2\text{ meetings}$$

$$g\left(7\right)=-42\neq-40$$

Meeting count and vertex height both match the rebuild, The stem produces $2$, not $3$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

The axis is the midpoint of the roots or $-b/(2a)$, not a one-unit shift.

$$x=7\neq8$$

The axis is $x=7$, not $x=8$, so the statement is False.

$$x=7$$

tasks.title: Mixed exam — WindFarm nesting
tasks.context: Composition drills for WindFarm: $f(x)=3 x + 1$, $g(x)=x^{2} - 4 x + 8$. Expand before trusting degree shortcuts. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: $g(f(x))$ has highest power $x^{2}$ with leading coefficient $9$, while $f(g(x))$ has highest power $x^{2}$ with leading coefficient $3$.
$g(f(x))$ has highest power $x^{3}$ because degrees add.
There exist $A,B,C$ with $g(x)=A f(x)^2+B f(x)+C$ and $A=\frac{1}{9}$.
$f(g(1))$ always equals $g(f(1))$ for every linear $f$ and quadratic $g$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Highest powers multiply under nesting; leading coefficients multiply by the outer map's lead and the inner lead raised to the outer degree.

$$g(f(x))=9 x^{2} - 6 x + 5$$

$$f(g(x))=3 x^{2} - 12 x + 25$$

$$\text{leads }9\text{ and }3$$

Degrees and leading coefficients of both orders match, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Highest powers multiply under nesting: $2\cdot 1=2$, they do not add.

$$g(f(x))=9 x^{2} - 6 x + 5$$

The top power is $x^{2}$, not $x^{3}$, so the statement is False.

$$\text{top power}=2$$

**C.** → True

Match coefficients in $A(mx+k)^{2}+B(mx+k)+C$.

$$A=\frac{1}{3^2}=\frac{1}{9}$$

$$B=-\frac{14}{9},\ C=\frac{85}{9}$$

$A=\frac{1}{9}$ is consistent, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

Evaluate the inner map first in each order; composition is not commutative.

$$f(1)=4,\quad g(f(1))=8$$

$$g(1)=5,\quad f(g(1))=16$$

Both nested evaluations match, The stem produces $1$, not $2$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

A single coincidence does not make a general law; the two orders differ here.

$$f(g(1))=16$$

$$g(f(1))=8$$

The orders need not agree in general, so the statement is False.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — IceRink factored read
tasks.context: IceRink stores clearance in factored form $g(x)=(x-1)(x-5)$. A tariff line is $f(x)=3 x - 2$. Read zeros, Vieta, and the vertex without expanding first. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The zeros read from the factors are $x=1$ and $x=5$.
By Vieta on the expanded form, the root sum equals $6$ and therefore the axis is $x=3$.
The axis of symmetry is $x=4$ because one root is shifted by one unit.
The product of the roots equals $-5$ (sign flipped from $c/a$).
At the left-hand zero $x=1$, the signed gap $f-g$ equals $1$, and the graphs meet in exactly 2 real points overall.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Each linear factor $x-r$ contributes a zero at $x=r$; the leading constant does not move the zeros.

$$g(x)=(x-1)(x-5)$$

$$g\left(1\right)=0,\quad g\left(5\right)=0$$

Both claimed zeros sit on the factors, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Vieta gives $S=-b/a$; the axis is the midpoint $S/2$.

$$g(x)=x^{2} - 6 x + 5$$

$$S=6$$

$$x_{\text{axis}}=3$$

Sum and axis agree with the factors, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

Shifting a single root would move the midpoint, but both roots are fixed; the axis stays at their average.

$$x=3\neq 4$$

The axis is $x=3$, not $x=4$, so the statement is False.

$$x=3$$

**D.** → False

Vieta gives $P=c/a$ with no extra minus; flipping the sign is a common exam trap.

$$P=5=1\cdot5$$

The product is $5$, not $-5$, so the statement is False.

$$P=5$$

**E.** → True

At a zero of $g$, the gap collapses to $f(r)$. Separately, meetings solve $g-f=0$.

$$f\left(1\right)-g\left(1\right)=1$$

$$g(x)-f(x)=x^{2} - 9 x + 7$$

$$\Delta=53\Rightarrow 2\text{ meetings}$$

Both the local gap and the global meeting count match, so the statement is True.

$$x=-4$$

$A=-\frac{1}{25}$, so the statement is True.

$$A=-\frac{1}{25}$$

$$\Delta=169$$

There are 2 meetings, not 4, so the statement is False.

$$f(0)-g(0)=0$$

The gap matches, so the statement is True.

**E.** → True

tasks.title: Mixed exam — CargoDrone dense scenarios
tasks.context: Chapter 7 mixed exam — CargoDrone batch 1. Each statement below is its own mini-scenario about lines or parabolas; no shared stem formulas. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: (i) For $p(x)=5 x^{2} - 3 x + 1$, the axis is $x=\frac{3}{10}$ and the vertex height is $\frac{11}{20}$.
(ii) A line with slope $3$ through $\left(2,11\right)$ is $y=3 x + 5$, but shifting the intercept by $1$ would still pass through the point.
(iii) For $q(x)=- 2 x^{2} + 6 x - 4$, the vertex occurs at $x=\frac{3}{2}$ with height $\frac{1}{2}$.
(iv) With $f(x)=x + 1$ and $g(x)=x \left(2 x - 3\right)$, the composition $g(f(x))$ has degree $3$.
(v) The roots of $x^{2} - 6 x + 5=0$ multiply to $-5$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Apply $x=-b/(2a)$ then evaluate $p$ there.

$$x=\frac{3}{10}$$

$$p\left(\frac{3}{10}\right)=\frac{11}{20}$$

Axis and height both match, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Point-slope reconstruction fixes both slope and intercept; changing the intercept moves the line off the given point.

$$y-11=3(x-2)\Rightarrow y=3 x + 5$$

$$y=3 x + 6\text{ misses }(2,11)$$

The intercept cannot be shifted without leaving the point, so the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Axis $x=-b/(2a)$; evaluate $q$ there for the height.

$$x=\frac{3}{2}$$

$$q\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)=\frac{1}{2}$$

Vertex abscissa and height match, so the statement is True.

**D.** → True

Degrees multiply under nesting.

$$g(f(x))=2 x^{2} + x - 1$$

$$\text{top power}=2\neq 3$$

The degree is $2$, not $3$, so the statement is True.

**E.** → True

Vieta: product $c/a$ with no extra minus sign.

$$P=5=1\cdot5$$

The product is $5$, not $-5$, so the statement is True.

$$P=5$$

Because $f$ is linear, $g(f(x))$ has highest power $x^3$ (degrees add under nesting).
The service line and clearance parabola meet in exactly 3 distinct real points.
Converting the axis gap to millimetres by multiplying by $10$ (not $1000$) gives $-210$ mm.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Locate the axis, subtract the heights in metres, then multiply by $100$ for centimetres — never convert before subtracting.

$$x=-2$$

$$f-g=-21\text{ m}$$

$$100(f-g)=-2100\text{ cm}$$

Metre gap and centimetre conversion both match, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Differentiate $R(x)=x(mx+k)$; the critical point $-k/(2m)$ is unrelated to the clearance axis $-b/(2a)$ unless coefficients accidentally match.

$$R(x)=2 x \left(2 x - 1\right)$$

$$R'(x)=0\Rightarrow x=\frac{1}{4}$$

$$\text{axis of }g:\ x=-2$$

Revenue peak and clearance axis need not coincide, so the statement is False.

**C.** → False

Under composition, highest powers multiply: $2\cdot 1=2$, they do not add.

$$g(f(x))=11 - 16 x^{2}$$

$$\text{top power}=2\neq 3$$

The highest power is $x^{2}$, not $x^{3}$, so the statement is False.

**D.** → False

Solve $g(x)=f(x)$ and read the discriminant of the difference.

$$g(x)-f(x)=- x^{2} - 8 x + 9$$

$$\Delta=100$$

There are 2 meetings, The stem produces $2$, not $3$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

One metre is $1000$ millimetres; multiplying by $10$ under-converts by a factor of $100$.

$$f-g=-21\text{ m}$$

$$1000(f-g)=-21000\text{ mm}\neq-210$$

The millimetre conversion factor is $1000$, not $10$, so the statement is False.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — symbolic reasoning 2
tasks.context: A line $f$ and a parabola $g$ are compared with the mirrored pair $\tilde f(x)=f(-x)$, $\tilde g(x)=g(-x)$. No coordinates are given. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The graphs of $\tilde f$ and $\tilde g$ meet exactly as often as those of $f$ and $g$.
If $f$ and $g$ are tangent, then so are $\tilde f$ and $\tilde g$.
Mirroring can turn two meetings into three.
$\tilde g$ opens in the same direction as $g$, if the leading coefficient is replaced by its opposite.
$\tilde g$ always has the same axis of symmetry as $g$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The mirror $x\mapsto -x$ is a bijection sending intersections to intersections.

$$x\text{ solves }g=f\iff -x\text{ solves }\tilde g=\tilde f$$

Meeting count is preserved, so the statement is True.

$$\#\text{meetings preserved}$$

**B.** → True

A double root is mirrored into a double root.

$$\Delta(g-f)=0\Rightarrow\Delta(\tilde g-\tilde f)=0$$

Tangency survives mirroring, so the statement is True.

$$\text{double root mirrored}$$

**C.** → False

The difference stays quadratic, so at most two real zeros.

$$\text{degree of }(\tilde g-\tilde f)=2$$

At most two meetings remain, so the statement is False.

$$\leq 2\text{ roots}$$

**D.** → False

Replacing $x$ by $-x$ leaves the leading coefficient unchanged.

$$a_{\tilde g}=a$$

Opening direction is preserved, Changing the leading-coefficient sign breaks the claim, so the statement is False.

$$\text{sign}(a)\text{ unchanged}$$

**E.** → False

The axis is reflected: $x\mapsto -x$ sends $x=h$ to $x=-h$ unless $h=0$.

$$x_{\tilde g}=-x_{g}$$

The axis moves unless it is the $y$-axis, so the statement is False.

$$x\mapsto -x$$

tasks.title: Mixed exam — MineCart parameter sweep
tasks.context: A one-parameter family $g_a(x)=ax^{2}+2x-3$ with $a\neq 0$ is tested against $f(x)=6 x$. Study how the parameter $a$ changes meetings via $\Delta(a)$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: There is a value of $a\neq 0$ for which the line is tangent to the parabola.
For every $a>-\frac{4}{3}$ the graphs meet twice.
Some $a\neq 0$ make the graphs miss entirely ($\Delta(a)<0$).
The axis of $g_a$ is the same for all $a$.
Every parabola in the family crosses the $y$-axis at $-3$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Tangency is $\Delta(a)=0$; solve for $a$ and discard $a=0$ if it appears.

$$\Delta(a)=12 a + 16$$

The discriminant vanishes for some $a\neq 0$, so the statement is True.

$$\Delta=12 a + 16$$

**B.** → False

A linear (or quadratic) discriminant in $a$ changes sign at most twice; an open half-line of parameters is not automatically a double-meeting zone.

$$\Delta(a)=12 a + 16$$

$$a=-\frac{4}{3}\text{ is a critical threshold, not a blanket guarantee}$$

The inequality range overstates where $\Delta>0$, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

Pick $a$ on the side of the critical root where the discriminant is negative.

$$\Delta(a)=12 a + 16$$

No real roots occur for some admissible $a$, so the statement is True.

$$\Delta<0\text{ for some }a$$

**D.** → False

The axis $x=-1/a$ moves when $a$ changes.

$$x_{\text{axis}}=-\frac{1}{a}$$

The axis depends on $a$, so the statement is False.

$$x=-1/a$$

**E.** → True

The constant term does not involve $a$.

$$g_a(0)=-3$$

The $y$-intercept is always $-3$, so the statement is True.

$$c=-3$$

tasks.title: Mixed exam — Orchard reconstruction
tasks.context: Engineers know a service line has slope $2$ and passes through $\left(2,5\right)$. The parabola has vertex $\left(5,-22\right)$ and leading coefficient $1$. Recover $f$ and $g$, then decide. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The rebuilt line is $f(x)=2 x + 1$, matching the sparse point-slope data.
Rewriting $g$ in powers of the rebuilt line gives $g(x)=A f(x)^2+B f(x)+C$ with $A=\frac{1}{4}$.
The same rewrite has leading coefficient $A=\frac{5}{4}$.
The rebuilt curves meet in exactly 2 distinct real points, and the vertex height is $-22$ (not $-20$).
The axis of the rebuilt parabola is $x=6$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Point-slope form: $f(x)=m(x-x_0)+y_0$.

$$f(x)=2 x + 1$$

The line matches the data, so the statement is True.

$$m=2$$

**B.** → True

Match coefficients in $A(mx+k)^{2}+B(mx+k)+C$ against the rebuilt pair.

$$A=\frac{1}{2^2}=\frac{1}{4}$$

$$B=-\frac{11}{2},\ C=\frac{33}{4}$$

$A=\frac{1}{4}$ is consistent with the rewrite, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

The rewrite leading coefficient is $a/m^{2}$, not an off-by-one guess.

$$A=\frac{1}{4}\neq\frac{5}{4}$$

The correct $A$ is $\frac{1}{4}$, so the statement is False.

$$A=\frac{1}{4}$$

**D.** → True

Solve $g=f$ for the meeting count, then evaluate $g$ on the axis for height.

$$\Delta=136\Rightarrow 2\text{ meetings}$$

$$g\left(5\right)=-22\neq-20$$

Meeting count and vertex height both match the rebuild, so the statement is True.

**E.** → True

The axis is the midpoint of the roots or $-b/(2a)$, not a one-unit shift.

$$x=5\neq6$$

The axis is $x=5$, not $x=6$, so the statement is True.

$$x=5$$

tasks.title: Mixed exam — BridgeDeck nesting
tasks.context: BridgeDeck control software nests $f$ and $g$ ($f(x)=3 x + 2$, $g(x)=- x^{2} - 12 x + 4$). Compare degrees, leading coefficients, and evaluations. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: $g(f(x))$ has highest power $x^{2}$ with leading coefficient $-9$, while $f(g(x))$ has highest power $x^{2}$ with leading coefficient $-3$.
$g(f(x))$ has highest power $x^{3}$ because degrees add.
There exist $A,B,C$ with $g(x)=A f(x)^2+B f(x)+C$ and $A=-\frac{1}{9}$.
$f(g(2))$ always equals $g(f(2))$ for every linear $f$ and quadratic $g$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Highest powers multiply under nesting; leading coefficients multiply by the outer map's lead and the inner lead raised to the outer degree.

$$g(f(x))=- 9 x^{2} - 48 x - 24$$

$$f(g(x))=- 3 x^{2} - 36 x + 14$$

$$\text{leads }-9\text{ and }-3$$

Degrees and leading coefficients of both orders match, so the statement is True.

**B.** → True

Highest powers multiply under nesting: $2\cdot 1=2$, they do not add.

$$g(f(x))=- 9 x^{2} - 48 x - 24$$

The top power is $x^{2}$, not $x^{3}$, so the statement is True.

$$\text{top power}=2$$

**C.** → True

Match coefficients in $A(mx+k)^{2}+B(mx+k)+C$.

$$A=\frac{-1}{3^2}=-\frac{1}{9}$$

$$B=-\frac{32}{9},\ C=\frac{104}{9}$$

$A=-\frac{1}{9}$ is consistent, so the statement is True.

**D.** → True

Evaluate the inner map first in each order; composition is not commutative.

$$f(2)=8,\quad g(f(2))=-156$$

$$g(2)=-24,\quad f(g(2))=-70$$

Both nested evaluations match, so the statement is True.

**E.** → True

A single coincidence does not make a general law; the two orders differ here.

$$f(g(2))=-70$$

$$g(f(2))=-156$$

The orders need not agree in general, so the statement is True.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — FloodGate factored read
tasks.context: Completed-square form for FloodGate: $g(x)=-\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)^{2}+\frac{25}{4}$. Service line $f(x)=2 x + 4$. Cross-check against the factored model $g(x)=-(x+3)(x-2)$. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: The zeros read from the factors are $x=-3$ and $x=2$.
By Vieta on the expanded form, the root sum equals $0$ and therefore the axis is $x=-\frac{1}{2}$.
The axis of symmetry is $x=\frac{1}{2}$ because one root is shifted by one unit.
The product of the roots equals $6$ (sign flipped from $c/a$).
At the left-hand zero $x=-2$, the signed gap $f-g$ equals $-2$, and the graphs meet in exactly 2 real points overall.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Each linear factor $x-r$ contributes a zero at $x=r$; the leading constant does not move the zeros.

$$g(x)=-(x+3)(x-2)$$

$$g\left(-3\right)=0,\quad g\left(2\right)=0$$

Both claimed zeros sit on the factors, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Vieta gives $S=-b/a$; the axis is the midpoint $S/2$.

$$g(x)=- x^{2} - x + 6$$

$$S=-1$$

$$x_{\text{axis}}=-\frac{1}{2}$$

Sum and axis agree with the factors, The stem produces $-1$, not $0$, so the statement is False.

**C.** → False

Shifting a single root would move the midpoint, but both roots are fixed; the axis stays at their average.

$$x=-\frac{1}{2}\neq \frac{1}{2}$$

The axis is $x=-\frac{1}{2}$, not $x=\frac{1}{2}$, so the statement is False.

$$x=-\frac{1}{2}$$

**D.** → False

Vieta gives $P=c/a$ with no extra minus; flipping the sign is a common exam trap.

$$P=-6=-3\cdot2$$

The product is $-6$, not $6$, so the statement is False.

$$P=-6$$

**E.** → False

At a zero of $g$, the gap collapses to $f(r)$. Separately, meetings solve $g-f=0$.

$$f\left(-3\right)-g\left(-3\right)=-2$$

$$g(x)-f(x)=- x^{2} - 3 x + 2$$

$$\Delta=17\Rightarrow 2\text{ meetings}$$

Both the local gap and the global meeting count match, The stem produces $-3$, not $-2$, so the statement is False.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — RaceTrack hybrid check
tasks.context: RaceTrack published a spot table (below) together with the formulas $g(x)=x^{2} - 4 x + 6$ and $f(x)=5 x - 5$. Mix table lookups with algebra. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: From the table, $g(2)=2$, matching the printed parabola.
The axis $x=2$ appears as a sample column; $g(2)=2$ matches the vertex height.
First differences of the $g$-row are constant, so $g$ is linear.
The curves meet in exactly 3 points, and at $x=0$ the gap is $-11$.
The slope of $f$ equals $6$ because the table's first $f$-step looks steeper.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Read the $x=2$ column, then substitute into $g$ as a cross-check.

$$g(2)=2$$

Table and formula agree at $x=2$, so the statement is True.

$$g(2)=2$$

**B.** → True

Form $-b/(2a)$ from coefficients; the table may or may not sample that abscissa.

$$x=2$$

$$g\left(2\right)=2$$

The axis claim is consistent with the coefficients, so the statement is True.

**C.** → False

A quadratic row has linearly growing first differences and constant second differences.

$$g(x)=x^{2} - 4 x + 6$$

Constant first differences would require a line, not $g$, so the statement is False.

$$\Delta^{{(1)}}\text{ not constant for }g$$

**D.** → False

Combine a discriminant count with an origin evaluation.

$$\Delta=37$$

$$f(0)-g(0)=-11$$

Meeting count and origin gap both match, The stem produces $2$, not $3$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

Read the coefficient of $x$ in the printed line; a single table step is not a slope trap.

$$f(x)=5 x - 5$$

$$m=5\neq6$$

The slope is $5$, so the statement is False.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — Observatory dense scenarios
tasks.context: Chapter 7 mixed exam — Observatory batch 2. Each statement below is its own mini-scenario about lines or parabolas; no shared stem formulas. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: (i) For $p(x)=5 x^{2} - 5 x + 2$, the axis is $x=\frac{1}{2}$ and the vertex height is $\frac{3}{4}$.
(ii) A line with slope $5$ through $\left(2,15\right)$ is $y=5 x + 5$, but shifting the intercept by $1$ would still pass through the point.
(iii) For $q(x)=- 2 x^{2} + 7 x - 4$, the vertex occurs at $x=\frac{7}{4}$ with height $\frac{17}{8}$.
(iv) With $f(x)=x + 2$ and $g(x)=2 x \left(x - 2\right)$, the composition $g(f(x))$ has degree $3$.
(v) The roots of $x^{2} - 8 x + 12=0$ multiply to $-12$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Apply $x=-b/(2a)$ then evaluate $p$ there.

$$x=\frac{1}{2}$$

$$p\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{3}{4}$$

Axis and height both match, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Point-slope reconstruction fixes both slope and intercept; changing the intercept moves the line off the given point.

$$y-15=5(x-2)\Rightarrow y=5 x + 5$$

$$y=5 x + 6\text{ misses }(2,15)$$

The intercept cannot be shifted without leaving the point, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

Axis $x=-b/(2a)$; evaluate $q$ there for the height.

$$x=\frac{7}{4}$$

$$q\left(\frac{7}{4}\right)=\frac{17}{8}$$

Vertex abscissa and height match, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

Degrees multiply under nesting.

$$g(f(x))=2 x \left(x + 2\right)$$

$$\text{top power}=2\neq 3$$

The degree is $2$, not $3$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

Vieta: product $c/a$ with no extra minus sign.

$$P=12=2\cdot6$$

The product is $12$, not $-12$, so the statement is True.

$$P=12$$

tasks.title: Mixed exam — Axis and Intercepts from the Sketch
tasks.context: The sketch shows how a linear tariff and a quadratic height cap interact for Harvester. Use the marked vertex and roots together with the geometry. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: From the plot, the parabola turns at $x=-4$ with height $24$, and by Vieta the root-sum of $g$ is $-8$ so the midpoint of the zeros also equals $-4$.
At the axis the signed gap $f-g$ equals $-37$, and therefore the graphs meet in exactly 0 real points.
The midpoint of the meeting abscissae (roots of $g-f$) equals $x=-5$, which differs from the parabola's own axis $x=-4$.
The axis of symmetry of the parabola is the horizontal line $y=25$.
Counting crossings in the figure, the graphs meet in exactly 3 real points, and the signed axis gap $f-g$ equals $-35$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Read the turning abscissa as $-b/(2a)$, evaluate height there, then confirm the same abscissa as half the Vieta sum of the zeros.

$$x=-\frac{b}{2a}=-\frac{-8}{2\cdot -1}=-4$$

$$g\left(-4\right)=24$$

$$S=-\frac{b}{a}=-8\Rightarrow\frac{S}{2}=-4$$

Vertex abscissa and Vieta midpoint agree, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

The gap on the axis and the meeting count are independent: evaluate $f-g$ at the axis first, then inspect the discriminant of $g-f$ separately.

$$f\left(-4\right)-g\left(-4\right)=-35\neq-37$$

$$g(x)-f(x)=- x^{2} - 10 x + 11$$

$$\Delta=144\Rightarrow 2\text{ meetings, not }0$$

Both halves of the compound claim fail, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

Meeting abscissae are roots of $d=g-f$; their midpoint is the axis of $d$, which shifts whenever the line has nonzero slope.

$$d(x)=- x^{2} - 10 x + 11$$

$$x_{\text{meet mid}}=-5,\quad x_{\text{axis of }g}=-4$$

The meeting midpoint and the parabola axis are compared correctly, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

A parabola $ax^{2}+bx+c$ has a vertical mirror $x=\text{constant}$; a horizontal $y$-line through the vertex height is not the axis.

$$x=-4$$

$$g\left(-4\right)=24$$

The axis is the vertical line $x=-4$, not $y=25$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

Combine the discriminant count with a direct height comparison on the axis.

$$\Delta=144\Rightarrow 2\text{ meetings}$$

$$f-g\big|_{x=-4}=-35$$

Both the meeting count and the axis gap match the figure, The stem produces $2$, not $3$, so the statement is False.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — ZipLine sequence
tasks.context: Quality control for ZipLine tracks $s_n$ below. Recover $a,b,c$ from the difference table before trusting the printed continuous models. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Reading $\Delta^{(2)}$ as constantly $2$ forces $a=1$; combining with $\Delta^{(1)}_0=-9$ and $s_0=2$ rebuilds $b=-10$, $c=2$, matching the continuous $g$.
Because the opening first difference equals $-9$, the slope of the continuous line $f$ must also equal $-9$.
After reconstruction, the axis of the discrete quadratic is $x=5$, identical to the axis of the continuous model $g$.
The second differences are constantly $3$, so the leading coefficient of $g$ would be $\frac{3}{2}$.
At $n=3$ the table entry $s_3$ equals $-19$, which agrees with the continuous evaluation $g(3)=-19$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Constant second differences equal $2a$; the opening first difference is $a+b$; the $n=0$ entry is $c$.

$$\Delta^{(2)}=2a=2\Rightarrow a=1$$

$$\Delta^{(1)}_0=a+b=-9\Rightarrow b=-10$$

$$s_0=c=2$$

The reconstructed triple matches the continuous quadratic, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

First differences of a quadratic sequence grow linearly; they are not the slope of the unrelated service line $f$.

$$\Delta^{(1)}_0=-9$$

$$f'(x)=3\neq-9$$

Confusing $\Delta^{{(1)}}$ with the slope of $f$ is a trap, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

Once $a$ and $b$ are recovered from the table, form $-b/(2a)$ and compare with the printed continuous axis.

$$x=-\frac{-10}{2\cdot 1}=5$$

$$\text{axis of }g=5$$

Discrete reconstruction and continuous model share the axis, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

Read the constant second-difference row carefully; twice that constant is $a$.

$$\Delta^{(2)}=2\neq3$$

$$a=\frac{\Delta^{(2)}}{2}=1$$

The constant is $2$, not $3$, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

Substitute into the reconstructed rule, then cross-check against $g(3)$.

$$s_3=1\cdot 9+-10\cdot 3+2=-19$$

$$g(3)=-19$$

Table entry and continuous evaluation agree, so the statement is True.

tasks.title: Mixed exam — symbolic reasoning 3
tasks.context: A quadratic $g(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ with $a\neq 0$ has two distinct real roots; write $S$ for their sum and $P$ for their product. No numbers are supplied. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: If $P<0$, the two roots have opposite signs.
If $P>0$ and $S<0$, both roots are negative.
If $P>0$, both roots must be positive.
If $S=0$, the roots are opposites and the axis is the $y$-axis.
If $P<0$ and $a>0$, then $g(0)<0$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

A negative product forces one root on each side of the origin.

$$r_{1}r_{2}=P<0$$

Opposite signs follow from $P<0$, so the statement is True.

$$P<0\Rightarrow\text{opposite signs}$$

**B.** → True

Equal signs from the product, negative from the sum.

$$P>0,S<0\Rightarrow r_{1},r_{2}<0$$

Both roots lie left of the origin, so the statement is True.

$$\text{same sign, negative}$$

**C.** → True

They could both be negative instead.

$$P>0,S<0\Rightarrow\text{both negative possible}$$

Positive product does not force positive roots, so the statement is True.

$$P>0\not\Rightarrow r>0$$

**D.** → True

A vanishing sum puts the midpoint of the roots at the origin.

$$S=0\Rightarrow h=0$$

The axis is $x=0$, so the statement is True.

$$x_{\text{axis}}=0$$

**E.** → True

$P=c/a$, so $c$ and $a$ have opposite signs when $P<0$.

$$g(0)=c<0\text{ when }a>0,P<0$$

The origin lies below the axis, so the statement is True.

$$c=Pa<0$$

tasks.title: Mixed exam — Substation parameter sweep
tasks.context: Lines $f_k(x)=x+k$ slide vertically against $g(x)=x^{2}-2x-5$. Decide which inequalities on $k$ force two meetings, tangency, or a miss. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: Exactly one value of $k$ gives tangency, namely $k=-\frac{29}{4}$.
Whenever $k<-\frac{29}{4}$, the line meets the parabola twice.
Whenever $k>-\frac{30}{4}$, the line meets the parabola twice.
When $k=2$ the line meets the parabola twice.
For every real $k$ the line meets the parabola.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Tangency is one equation in $k$ from $\Delta(k)=0$.

$$\Delta(k)=4 k + 29$$

$$k=-\frac{29}{4}$$

The discriminant is linear in $k$ with one real root, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Read the sign of the leading coefficient of $\Delta(k)$ before choosing which side of the critical value gives $\Delta>0$.

$$\Delta(k)=4 k + 29$$

$$\Delta>0\text{ on the side }k>-\frac{29}{4}\text{, not }k<-\frac{29}{4}$$

The inequality points the wrong way, so the statement is False.

**C.** → False

On the side of $k={F(k_star)}$ where $\Delta(k)$ keeps the sign of its leading coefficient, two distinct real meetings occur.

$$\Delta(k)=4 k + 29$$

$$k>-\frac{29}{4}\Rightarrow\Delta(k)>0$$

tasks.context: A line $f(x)=3 x + 3$ and parabola $g(x)=x^{2} - 8 x + 7$ are nested in both orders. Track highest powers, leads, and a sample value. Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: $g(f(x))$ has highest power $x^{2}$ with leading coefficient $9$, while $f(g(x))$ has highest power $x^{2}$ with leading coefficient $3$.
$g(f(x))$ has highest power $x^{3}$ because degrees add.
There exist $A,B,C$ with $g(x)=A f(x)^2+B f(x)+C$ and $A=\frac{1}{9}$.
$f(g(3))$ always equals $g(f(3))$ for every linear $f$ and quadratic $g$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Highest powers multiply under nesting; leading coefficients multiply by the outer map's lead and the inner lead raised to the outer degree.

$$g(f(x))=9 x^{2} - 6 x - 8$$

$$f(g(x))=3 x^{2} - 24 x + 24$$

$$\text{leads }9\text{ and }3$$

Degrees and leading coefficients of both orders match, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Highest powers multiply under nesting: $2\cdot 1=2$, they do not add.

$$g(f(x))=9 x^{2} - 6 x - 8$$

The top power is $x^{2}$, not $x^{3}$, so the statement is False.

$$\text{top power}=2$$

**C.** → True

Match coefficients in $A(mx+k)^{2}+B(mx+k)+C$.

$$A=\frac{1}{3^2}=\frac{1}{9}$$

$$B=-\frac{10}{3},\ C=16$$

$A=\frac{1}{9}$ is consistent, so the statement is True.

**D.** → True

Evaluate the inner map first in each order; composition is not commutative.

$$f(3)=12,\quad g(f(3))=55$$

$$g(3)=-8,\quad f(g(3))=-21$$

Both nested evaluations match, so the statement is True.

**E.** → False

A single coincidence does not make a general law; the two orders differ here.

$$f(g(3))=-21$$

$$g(f(3))=55$$

The orders need not agree in general, so the statement is False.
